title: Quantization: int8, FP8, 4-bit and GGUF
hook: Plant a few large weights and watch int8 with one scale fall apart, while a scale per 32 weights and FP8 shrug it off.

verified.claim: The registry of formats and their layouts is in QUANT_ALGOS and QUANTIZATION.md.
Formats a device cannot compute are dequantized for the matmul, and the split is logged as native and emulated ops.
Core's model folders do not accept .gguf, and main.py warns GGUF users when dynamic VRAM is turned off.
The Q8_0 and Q4_0 round trips follow the ggml reference quantizers.
Error figures in the Lab come from a run here on synthetic weights.

unchecked: How much any format changes a real picture, and which format is fastest on a given card. This lesson measures weight and matmul error only.
The speed statement about native formats in main.py is the developers' own, and we did not test it.
